html:
The Suez Canal Company was the French-led company formed in 1858 by Ferdinand de Lesseps to build and run the Suez Canal in Egypt.

Lesseps won a concession from Egypt's ruler Said Pasha. The company sold shares mostly in France, and Egypt took a large stake. Egyptian peasants were drafted to dig in the early years. The canal opened in 1869 and the company earned tolls under a 99-year lease.

Egypt's debts forced Ismail Pasha to sell his shares to Britain in 1875, and Britain occupied Egypt in 1882, partly to guard the route to India. The company stayed a symbol of foreign control. In July 1956 Nasser nationalised it to pay for the Aswan High Dam, which set off the Suez Crisis. The company lived on in France as an investment firm.
sum: The Suez Canal Company was the French-led company formed in 1858 by Ferdinand de Lesseps to build and run the Suez Canal in Egypt.
